experiments.name: MIL-STD-883 Method 1010.8 temperature cycling, test condition C (-65 C to +150 C, at least 10 cycles, at least 10 min dwell)
experiments.plain_name: Check that sealed military-grade chips survive repeated swings between -65 C and +150 C
experiments.description: Microcircuit screening/qualification by air-to-air temperature cycling per MIL-STD-883 Method 1010.8: a minimum of 10 uninterrupted cycles of test condition C, cold step -65 C (+0/-10) and hot step +150 C (+15/-0), dwell at least 10 min, load reaching temperature within 15 min (16 min for a single chamber), followed by visual examination and end-point electrical tests.

requirements.rationale: Condition C cold step is -65 C (+0/-10), so the working zone must reach -65 C = 208.15 K or colder (third column of the cold row; columns are conditions A-F).
requirements.document_title: MIL-STD-883G Test Method 1010.8, Temperature Cycling (18 June 2004)
requirements.location: p. 2, Table I 'Temperature-cycling test conditions', step 1 (Cold), condition C column (text as extracted, columns A to F)

requirements.rationale: Condition C hot step is +150 C (+15/-0), so the chamber must reach +150 C = 423.15 K or hotter (third column of the hot row).
requirements.document_title: MIL-STD-883G Test Method 1010.8, Temperature Cycling (18 June 2004)
requirements.location: p. 2, Table I, step 2 (Hot), condition C column (text as extracted, columns A to F)

requirements.rationale: Optional single-chamber check: the load must traverse the 215 K span (+150 C to -65 C) within 16 min, i.e. on average at least 215 K / 16 min = 13.4375 K/min; a two-zone chamber satisfies the 1 min transfer instead.
requirements.document_title: MIL-STD-883G Test Method 1010.8, Temperature Cycling (18 June 2004)
requirements.quote: the dwell time shall not be less than 10 minutes and the load shall reach the specified temperature within 15 minutes (16 minutes for single chamber).

experiments.name: DC transfer characterization of commercial 5 nm n/p-FinFETs from 300 K down to 10 K on a closed-cycle cryogenic probe station
experiments.plain_name: Measure how the tiniest commercial transistors behave when cooled to 10 K
experiments.description: Ids-Vgs transfer curves (Vds 50 mV and 750 mV) of minimum-length multi-fin 5 nm FinFETs probed directly on their gate, source, drain and bulk pads in a Lake Shore CRX-VF closed-cycle cryogenic probe station from 300 K to 10 K with a Keysight B1500A; the data calibrate a cryogenic-aware BSIM-CMG compact model.

requirements.rationale: Transistors were measured over the whole span from 300 K down to 10 K (10 K was the lowest stable temperature with probes landed).
requirements.document_title: Design Automation for Cryogenic CMOS Circuits (van Santen et al., DAC 2023, doi:10.1109/DAC56929.2023.10247824)
requirements.location: Section II.B 'Measuring 5 nm FinFET Transistors for the Temperature Range'
requirements.quote: The heat flux from the probes introduces thermal fluctuations in the range of 3.5 K to 8.5 K. Therefore, the temperature 10 K is chosen as the lower limit because it is the smallest stable temperature.

requirements.rationale: The probed die sits in the evacuated sample space of the probe station.
requirements.document_title: Design Automation for Cryogenic CMOS Circuits (van Santen et al., DAC 2023, doi:10.1109/DAC56929.2023.10247824)
requirements.quote: The cryogenic probe station features a 51 mm diameter sample stage, a vacuum pump, a twostage closed-cycle refrigerator unit, and a probe handler/positioner.

requirements.rationale: Each transistor terminal (gate, source, drain, bulk) is contacted by its own probe, so four probe arms are needed.
requirements.document_title: Design Automation for Cryogenic CMOS Circuits (van Santen et al., DAC 2023, doi:10.1109/DAC56929.2023.10247824)
requirements.quote: in which the probes are placed on top of the measurement pads for each transistor terminal (i.e., gate, source, drain, bulk).

requirements.rationale: The DUT is biased and measured by the B1500A through the probes.
requirements.document_title: Design Automation for Cryogenic CMOS Circuits (van Santen et al., DAC 2023, doi:10.1109/DAC56929.2023.10247824)
requirements.quote: a semiconductor measurement station "Keysight's B1500A" is utilized to stimulate each transistor under measurement (i.e., apply the required voltage biases) and, then, measure its electrical response.

requirements.rationale: Optional: the source used a two-stage closed-cycle refrigerator rather than a liquid cryogen.
requirements.document_title: Design Automation for Cryogenic CMOS Circuits (van Santen et al., DAC 2023, doi:10.1109/DAC56929.2023.10247824)
requirements.quote: It consists of a cryogenic probe station "Lakeshore CRX-VF", a closed-cycle refrigerator, and a semiconductor measurement station "Keysight's B1500A".

sources.citation: Design Automation for Cryogenic CMOS Circuits (van Santen et al., DAC 2023, doi:10.1109/DAC56929.2023.10247824)

experiments.name: Automated full-wafer cryogenic probing of Si/SiGe spin-qubit devices on 300 mm wafers (chuck 1.0 K, electron temperature 1.6 K)
experiments.plain_name: Test hundreds of qubit chips across a whole 300 mm silicon wafer cooled near absolute zero
experiments.description: Intel's 300 mm Si/SiGe quantum-dot devices are cooled as whole wafers in a cryogenic wafer prober to a 1.0 K chuck base temperature (1.6 K electron temperature); pads (100 x 100 um, 150 um pitch) are aligned to probe pins by machine vision and gate-line resistance, threshold voltage, mobility and single-electron transitions are measured automatically across the wafer.

requirements.rationale: The procedure ran with the wafer chuck at its 1.0 K base, giving the 1.6 K electron temperature used to resolve single-electron transitions and to validate superconducting gate layers.
requirements.document_title: Probing single electrons across 300 mm spin qubit wafers (Neyens et al., arXiv:2307.04812; Nature 2024)
requirements.location: Main text, paragraph introducing the cryo-prober (Fig. 1)
requirements.quote: The cryo-prober can load and cool 300 mm wafers to a base temperature of 1.0 K at the chuck and an electron temperature of 1.6 ± 0.2 K (see Extended Data Fig. 2) in 2 hrs.

requirements.rationale: Whole 300 mm wafers are loaded and probed.
requirements.document_title: Probing single electrons across 300 mm spin qubit wafers (Neyens et al., arXiv:2307.04812; Nature 2024)
requirements.quote: Here we present a testing process using a cryogenic 300 mm wafer prober [13] to collect high-volume data on the performance of hundreds of industry-manufactured spin qubit devices at 1.6 K.

requirements.rationale: Device pads are contacted by probe pins wired to room-temperature sources and detectors.
requirements.document_title: Probing single electrons across 300 mm spin qubit wafers (Neyens et al., arXiv:2307.04812; Nature 2024)
requirements.location: Main text, paragraph introducing the cryo-prober
requirements.quote: The wafer is brought into contact with the probe pins to electrically connect device pads to voltage sources and current and voltage detectors at room temperature.

sources.citation: Probing single electrons across 300 mm spin qubit wafers (Neyens et al., arXiv:2307.04812; Nature 2024)

experiments.name: Conventional DLTS (100-420 K, 3 K/min) and Laplace-DLTS of the Z1/2 carbon-vacancy trap in 4H-SiC Schottky barrier diodes
experiments.plain_name: Find carbon-vacancy defects in silicon-carbide power diodes by scanning them from cold to hot
experiments.description: Ni/4H-SiC Schottky barrier diodes on 25 um nitrogen-doped epilayers are scanned by conventional DLTS from 100 K to 420 K at 3 K/min (Vr -10 V, 1 ms pulses, 50 s-1 rate window); isothermal Laplace-DLTS near 325-330 K and 220-260 K then resolves the Z1 and Z2 components and their acceptor levels.

requirements.rationale: The DLTS temperature scan covered 100-420 K.

requirements.quote: The DLTS measurements were performed in the temperature range 100-420 K at a ramp rate 3 K/min, reverse bias Vr = -10 V, pulse bias Vp = 0 V, pulse width tp = 1 ms and using a rate window of 50 s-1.

requirements.rationale: Optional: the published scan ramped at 3 K/min.

requirements.quote: The estimated error of the temperature used in the L-DLTS measurements was less than 0.1 K.

requirements.rationale: The diode is reverse biased and pulsed while its capacitance transient is recorded.

experiments.name: Functional test of an RSFQ digital-SQUID ADC with TFF and cumulative counters (AIST HSTP Nb process) at 4.2 K in a pulse-tube cryocooler
experiments.plain_name: Run a superconducting digital chip at 4.2 K to check that its logic works
experiments.description: A wire-bonded SFQ chip (digital-SQUID modulators, majority logic, toggle flip-flop and cumulative counters) is cooled to 4.2 K in a two-stage closed-cycle pulse-tube cryostat with a vibration-damping stage; separate DC bias rails from a HYPRES current source, clock through a bias-tee on RF-shielded coax, outputs amplified and checked on an oscilloscope and logic analyser.

requirements.rationale: The niobium SFQ circuit is operated at 4.2 K.

requirements.quote: a two-stage closed-cycle cryogenic system was employed, capable of achieving a base temperature of 4.2 K after an initial precooling stage at approximately 35 K.

requirements.quote: Separate DC bias lines were provided for the DC/SFQ, SFQ/DC, and main power rails to isolate functional blocks and minimize cross-interference.
